question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer is the IM of Lotus Infrastructure AIF (Cat I). He is explaining to a prospective LP why Management Fees continue to accrue even in a year when the fund books a loss. Which statement is the correct rationale under standard Indian AIF fee-structure doctrine?

answer.text: Management Fees are contingent on profits and are waived when the fund has a down year
Management Fees in a loss year are automatically clawed back at fund wind-up
Management Fees are recovered from the Sponsor's skin-in-the-game commitment in a loss year
Management Fees are paid for fund-management services rendered and are independent of gains or losses of the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 states Management Fee is FIXED and paid to the IM for services rendered, IRRESPECTIVE of future gains or losses of the fund. It compensates service, not performance. Performance-sensitivity sits in the Carry / Incentive Fee bucket. The Trap: Option A confuses management fee with performance fee; Option C invents a sponsor-recovery mechanic that does not exist in Indian AIF practice; Option D confuses management fee with carry clawback (clawback applies to performance fees only). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same principle without restricting to Cat I/II. In XXI-B (PMS), SEBI permits only a fixed fee or performance-linked fee (or combination), but PMS does not commingle capital — so the billing base differs from AIF. Manager's Pro-Tip: Use this clarification in LP pitches: position management fee as an 'operating retainer' for the IM team's lights-on cost (analysts, IC, legal, valuation). Pair it with a clear carry disclosure and LPs perceive better alignment than quoting a bundled '2 and 20' headline.
